option.approach: Audit whether quasitracial ultrapowers preserve all the hypotheses in the problem. If they do, compare the ultrapower elements represented by (a_n) and (a_{n+1}); their quasitraces agree while their positive difference has quasitrace η.

options.counterfactual: A faithful normalized 2-quasitrace on a finite AW*-factor need not be strictly order preserving: positive elements x<y can have equal quasitrace values.
options.approach: Audit the claimed strict-order theorem and separate faithfulness from strict order preservation. Retain only justified consequences, including the upper bound eta≤1/2 and downward closure of the admissible set.

options.counterfactual: A faithful normalized 2-quasitrace on a finite AW*-factor need not be strictly order preserving: positive elements x<y can have equal quasitrace values.
options.approach: Investigate the endpoint eta=1/2 using the more restricted question whether positive contractions x,y with x+y≤1 and quasitrace 1/2 each can satisfy quasitrace(x+y)=1/2. Excluding this particular absorption phenomenon would exclude the endpoint without requiring general strict order preservation.

options.counterfactual: Taking bounded sequences modulo sequences whose squared quasitraces tend to zero along an ultrafilter does not automatically produce a finite AW*-factor with a faithful normalized 2-quasitrace.
options.approach: Audit the quotient construction one hypothesis at a time: the ideal property, descent of the quasitrace, additivity on commuting quotient elements, the matrix extension, the annihilator property, and factoriality. Identify the first step that needs an additional theorem.

options.counterfactual: Taking bounded sequences modulo sequences whose squared quasitraces tend to zero along an ultrafilter does not automatically produce a finite AW*-factor with a faithful normalized 2-quasitrace.
options.approach: Avoid the quotient and seek a quantitative order estimate directly in the original factor. An estimate forcing the quasitrace of y−x to become small when the quasitraces of positive contractions x≤y become close would rule out constant positive increments.
